extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, EPA regional staff, electric generating unit (EGU) owners/operators, and electric reliability authorities (RTOs/ISOs/FERC)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for EGU owners/operators (and states) to request short-term extensions of enforceable cease-operation dates on reliability grounds under the final EPA emission guidelines, including required analyses, certifications, timelines, and documentation. Focused on demonstrating a documented reliability need for up to 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism purpose and scope (eligibility of units)
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism is for existing sources that have relied on a commitment to cease operating for purposes of these emission guidelines. Such reliance might occur in three circumstances: (1) units that plan to cease operation before January 1, 2032 and that are therefore exempt because they have elected to have enforceable cease operations dates in the state plan; (2) affected EGUs that choose to employ 40 percent natural gas co-firing by 2030 with a retirement date of no later than January 1, 2039; or (3) affected EGUs that have source-specific standards of performance based on remaining useful life, pursuant to the RULOF provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism allows extensions of enforceable cease-operation dates to address unforeseen reliability or reserve margin concerns that arise after a state plan is finalized. The date from which an extension can be given is the enforceable cease operations date in the state plan, including dates prior to January 1, 2032.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not applicable for certain delays or obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism is not intended for use with units encountering unforeseen delays in installation of control technologies, as such issues are addressed through compliance flexibilities discussed elsewhere, or for units subject to an obligation to operate that is not based on the reliability criteria included here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this mechanism to address construction/installation delays or contractual/operational obligations that are unrelated to documented electric reliability needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite compliance with milestones and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Only owners/operators of units that have satisfied all applicable milestones, metrics, and reporting obligations outlined in section X.C.3., and section X.C.4 for units with cease operation dates prior to January 1, 2032, may use this mechanism for an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units that have failed to meet these obligations must pursue extensions via the state plan revision process. Meeting these prerequisites ensures the state and public have information to assess whether the unit diligently took actions necessary to meet its enforceable cease operations date.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion to include mechanism in state plans
rubrics_metrics.description: States can decide whether to include this extension mechanism in their state plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a state includes the option, it may also impose additional requirements on units requesting extensions. The mechanism is optional for states and may be tailored by states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger and submission recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism would be triggered when a unit submits an application to the EPA Regional Administrator where it faces an unforeseen situation that creates a reliability issue should that unit go offline consistent with its commitment to cease operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the application should also be submitted to the state. For extension requests exceeding 6 months, an identical copy must be submitted to FERC through a process and office of FERC's designation (including any additional information FERC identifies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing windows and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: No less than 30 days prior to the compliance date for applications for extensions of less than 6 months, and no less than 45 days prior to the compliance date for applications for extensions exceeding 6 months, but no earlier than 12 months prior to the compliance date (requests over 12 months prior should be addressed through state plan revisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect these minimum lead times; requests submitted earlier than 12 months prior must be handled via state plan revision. Copy to FERC is required for >6 month requests and must follow FERC's submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven required application elements (overall requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written complete application must be submitted responding to each of the seven elements listed (elements 1–7) to activate the reliability assurance mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete submissions may be rejected by the EPA Regional Office within 30 days if missing required information or if the reliability assertion is not adequately supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 1 — Analysis of reliability risk if unit were not in operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis demonstrating that continued operation of the unit after the applicable compliance date is critical to maintaining electric reliability, such that retirement of that unit would (A) result in noncompliance with at least one mandatory reliability standard approved by FERC, or (B) cause the loss of load expectation to increase beyond the level targeted by regional system planners; requires clear demonstration that each unit would be needed to maintain targeted level of resource adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a projection substantiating the duration of the requested extension with accompanying analysis supporting the timeframe (not to exceed 12 months). Any unit with a Reliability Must Run Designation or equivalent would fit this description. Helpful information includes system planning and operations studies, system restoration studies or plans, operating procedures, and mitigation plans required by applicable Reliability Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 2 — Planning Authority analysis or concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis submitted by the relevant Planning Authority that verifies the reliability-related claims, or presents a separate and equivalent analysis, confirming the asserted reliability risk if the unit were not in operation, or an explanation of why such a concurrence or separate analysis cannot be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This analysis or concurrence must include substantiation for the duration of the extension request. If the Planning Authority cannot provide concurrence, the application must explain why and provide any related system-wide or regional analysis as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 3 — Third-party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of any written comments from third parties regarding the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all known written third-party input to allow the EPA and public to assess stakeholder views on the asserted reliability need and proposed extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 4 — Mitigation/plan to resolve underlying reliability issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration from the unit owner/operator, grid operator and other relevant entities that they have a plan that includes appropriate actions, including bringing on new capacity or transmission, to resolve the underlying reliability issue, including the steps and timeframes for implementing measures to rectify the underlying reliability issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show concrete, time-bound steps and responsible parties for how the identified reliability gap will be addressed during or after the extension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 5 — Duration limitation and increment-based granting
rubrics_metrics.description: Retirement date extensions allowed through this mechanism will be granted for only the increment of time that is substantiated by the reliability need and supporting documentation and may not exceed 12 months, inclusive of the 6-month extensions available with RTO, ISO, and reliability coordinator certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are strictly limited to the demonstrated necessary timeframe; the six-month extension available via RTO/ISO/certification counts toward the 12-month maximum. Any request for relief exceeding 12 months must be addressed through a state plan revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 6 — Optional state-required identification of operation level and alternative compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: States may choose to require the application to identify the level of operation that is required to avoid the documented reliability risk, and consistent with that level propose alternative compliance requirements, such as alternative standards or consistent utilization constraints for the duration of the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If states include this in their plan, applicants should propose (for the extension period) alternative standards or utilization constraints that reflect the minimal operation needed to avoid the reliability risk. The EPA Regional Office may reject incomplete or unsupported applications within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 7 — Eligibility limited to units meeting milestone/reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Only owners/operators of units that have satisfied all applicable milestone and reporting requirements and obligations under section X.C.3., and section X.C.4 for units with cease operation dates prior to January 1, 2032, may use this mechanism for an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units that failed to meet obligations may still request relief but must do so through state plan revision. This element ensures applicants have used available tools and complied with commitments before requesting short-term relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning Authority certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is requiring that the unit's relevant reliability Planning Authority(ies) certify that the claims are accurate and that the identified reliability problem both exists and requires the specific relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification from the Planning Authority is a required assurance; EPA will assess whether that certification and supporting analysis identify and support, in a detailed and reasoned fashion, anticipated noncompliance with a Reliability Standard or increased LOLE as substantiated by specific metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA consultation with FERC and other experts
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA intends to seek the advice of FERC for applications requesting more than 6 months of additional operating time and may also seek advice from other reliability experts to inform its decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will consult FERC to incorporate an expert reliability review; for >6 month requests, a copy must be provided to FERC through its designated process and office, and FERC may identify additional specific information to be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA decision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA intends to decide whether it will grant a compliance extension for a retiring unit based on a documented reliability need within 30 days of receiving the application for applications less than 6 months, and within 45 days for applications exceeding 6 months to account for time needed to consult with FERC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These timelines account for internal review and external consultation; applicants should expect decisions within these windows but must ensure submissions are complete to avoid rejection or delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision authority — EPA Regional Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to grant an extension to an owner/operator is solely the decision of the EPA Regional Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with Planning Authority certification and FERC advice, the ultimate approval authority for an extension under this mechanism is the Regional Administrator; states may not unilaterally grant extensions under the federal mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and documentation types helpful for demonstrating reliability need
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of information that will be helpful include, but are not limited to, system planning and operations studies, system restoration studies or plans, operating procedures, and mitigation plans required by applicable Reliability Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide robust, quantitative, regionally-contextualized studies and documentation to support assertions such as projected LOLE increases or potential noncompliance with mandatory reliability standards; RMR designations or equivalent supportive documentation are especially persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on purpose — only for situations insufficient time for state plan revision
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism creates additional flexibility for specified narrow circumstances for existing sources and provides additional time and flexibility to allow a state, if necessary, to submit a plan revision. In other words, this mechanism would be for use only when there is insufficient time to complete a state plan revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reliability concerns are identified more than one year in advance or otherwise allow time to pursue a state plan revision, the applicant should pursue the state plan revision path rather than this short-term mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and EPA cross-rule harmonization consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism is designed to be similar to backstop/reliability mechanisms used in other EPA rules (e.g., ELG) to harmonize emergency-related reliability criteria across rules and streamline demonstrations and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may leverage documentation and demonstrations previously prepared for other EPA emergency or reliability exemption processes to support consistency and streamline review.
